314	  `[S_H┬╖G_cal](t) / [S_H┬╖G_cal](t_0)` is the radiation-monitoring
315	  quantity of interest and is insensitive to the ambient field entirely.
316	- **Bias: no ΓÇö structurally.** The DC null survives every AC injection
317	  (CASE E): a Hall offset is observationally identical to a static
318	  ambient shift. Toggled DC injection (`┬▒I_cal,DC`, difference of
319	  states) measures *gain at the DC operating point* ΓÇö the difference
320	  `╬öy_H = 2┬╖S_H┬╖G_cal┬╖I_cal,DC` cancels both `b_H` and static ambient ΓÇö
321	  but never `b_H` itself. Offset requires zero-field/known-field epochs
322	  (MVD anchor ii) or an absolute reference. **Any design document
323	  claiming an embedded winding "calibrates the offset" is wrong**
324	  (Derived, Theorem 1 ╬▓-direction).
325	- Ambient variation *during* a toggle period leaks into the toggle
326	  difference; mitigation is fast square-wave toggling with synchronous
327	  demod, with the main coil as a dB/dt witness to gate/correct toggle
328	  epochs (Derived).
329	
330	### 5.2 Frequency plan and lock-in detection (Derived design rules)
331	
332	- Place `f_inj` in the **overlap band**: above the drift band `╧ë_d`,
333	  below the Hall pole, inside the coil's flat response ΓÇö
334	  `╧ë_d < 2╧Ç┬╖f_inj < min(a_Hall, ╧ë_C,max)` ΓÇö and in a measured-quiet
335	  region of the ambient spectrum. Spectral collision with ambient
336	  content re-creates the rank deficiency (CASE E-collide: 5/7) ΓÇö this is
337	  a hard requirement, not a preference. Machine EMI lines (power
338	  supplies, spinning-current harmonics) must be surveyed first
339	  (Hall-sensor EMI susceptibility is documented in adjacent contexts,
340	  [P021], [P022], C30).
341	- Coding (PRBS or slow frequency hopping) or on/off toggling makes the
342	  orthogonality verifiable: the estimator checks that the demodulated
343	  output tracks the injection schedule (loss-of-injection and
344	  collision-detection test in fault bank S4).
345	- Lock-in variance (first-order, matched-filter): for a sine injection
346	  of amplitude `B_a = G_cal┬╖I_a`,
347	  `var(┼£_H┬╖G_cal) Γëê 2╧â_H┬▓ / (T_int ┬╖ I_a┬▓┬╖G_cal┬▓)` ΓÇö integration time
348	  `T_int` trades against the drift timescale being tracked
349	  (quasi-stationarity window, stage-20 assumption 3). Choose `T_int` Γë¬
350	  expected drift correlation time; since GaN drift magnitudes are
351	  Unknown (C14), `T_int` is a *scheduled parameter*, revisited after
352	  validation rung 5 data exists.
353	- Coil-side lock-in: the coil sees `d(B_inj)/dt`, amplitude
354	  `Γê¥ ╧ë_inj┬╖B_a`, so coil-side SNR *improves* with frequency ΓÇö favoring
355	  the upper part of the allowed band, jointly optimized against the Hall
356	  pole margin (case 9: injecting near the pole additionally identifies
357	  Hall dynamics; CASE H-broad).
358	
359	### 5.3 Amplitude, heating, EMI (Derived design constraints)
360	
361	- **Amplitude floor:** `B_a` must give usable lock-in SNR within `T_int`
362	  (formula above) at the Hall noise floor.
363	- **Heating ceiling (self-interference):** winding dissipation
364	  `P_cal = I_rms┬▓┬╖R_cal` raises die temperature by `╬öT_die = R_th┬╖P_cal`,
365	  which enters the very term (`╬▒_S┬╖╬öT`) the system is trying to
366	  monitor. Self-consistency condition:
367	  `|╬▒_S| ┬╖ R_th ┬╖ R_cal ┬╖ I_rms┬▓ Γë¬ ╬┤_S` (target relative-gain
368	  resolution). This couples winding resistance, thermal design, and
369	  amplitude; it is a bench-characterizable inequality (Tier 1), and a
370	  reason the winding cannot simply be driven harder to buy SNR.
371	- **EMI/coupling:** the injection tone couples into the main coil by
372	  mutual inductance ΓÇö this is *used* (┬º5.5), but also contaminates the
373	  coil's field measurement at `f_inj`; the demodulator must notch the
374	  injection line out of the field-estimation path. Injection leads must
375	  be twisted/guarded so the *cable*, not just the winding, does not
376	  radiate (RIEMF and pickup discipline as for the main coil, C19).
377	- Under radiation, the cal circuit itself is exposed: RIEMF adds an
378	  error current/EMF in the injection loop ([R056] mechanism; Inferred
379	  transfer ΓÇö flagged, risk RR-12), and insulation leakage changes the
380	  delivered `I_cal` unless the readback shunt sits electrically close to
381	  the winding (design rule: **sense at the winding, not at the source**).
382	
383	### 5.4 The winding's own reference problem (stage-required; Derived)
384	
385	`G_cal` is geometry + magnetics. The stage forbids assuming it stays
386	known, and the evidence supports the caution: **no measurement of
387	radiation-induced coil-constant/effective-area drift exists for any
388	coil** (radiation review ┬º4 gap; metrology baseline [R069], [R070]), and
389	thermal expansion alone changes `G_cal` at the `╬▒_thermal┬╖╬öT` level.
390	Consequences:
391	
392	1. Only the **products** `S_H┬╖G_cal`, `K_C┬╖G_cal` are identifiable
393	   (CASE E). A reference-chain drift is indistinguishable from sensor
394	   gain drift *within the winding system alone*.
395	2. The JET RHP record shows the strength and the limit of the same-die
396	   approach: 11.5 years, SD Γëê 0.07 % sensitivity stability across
397	   >19,000 pulses including D-T ([H003], [H007], C05) ΓÇö but a co-located
398	   same-technology reference cannot by construction detect common-mode
399	   (shared radiation/thermal) drift of die and winding together (C05
400	   limitation). Mechanism diversity (geometric constant vs semiconductor
401	   transport) makes common-mode drift *physically unlikely* but not
402	   logically excluded (Inferred, stage-20 ┬º5.5).
403	3. **Resolution in this architecture: triangulation, not trust.** The
404	   winding is itself referenced against the machine-model anchor at
405	   every vacuum-shot epoch (CASE D identifies `S_H` and `K_C`
406	   absolutely; combined with the lock-in products this *solves for
407	   `G_cal` at each anchor epoch* ΓÇö Derived). Between anchors, `G_cal`
408	   drift is bounded by the closure test below, and its residual drift
409	   rate enters the uncertainty budget explicitly (┬º6.3) rather than
410	   being assumed zero.
411	
412	### 5.5 Triangle-closure consistency test (Derived; added design feature)
413	
414	The three continuously-available quantities
415	
416	```text
417	╧ü_HC   = S_H/K_C            (ambient AC cross-regression, CASE A invariant)
418	╧Ç_H    = S_H┬╖G_cal          (Hall-side lock-in)
419	╧Ç_C    = K_C┬╖G_cal          (coil-side lock-in)
420	```
421	
422	satisfy the identity `╧Ç_H / ╧Ç_C Γëí ╧ü_HC` for all t. The **closure
423	residual** `╬╡_╬ö = ╧Ç_H/╧Ç_C ΓêÆ ╧ü_HC` is measurable continuously and must be
424	zero to within noise regardless of drift in any single quantity.
425	`╬╡_╬ö Γëá 0` indicts the *measurement paths* (demodulator fault, spectral
426	collision, coil nonlinearity at `f_inj`, injection-line contamination) ΓÇö
427	a fault-detection channel that costs nothing extra. Note what it cannot
428	do: closure holds identically under any {`S_H`, `K_C`, `G_cal`} drift,
429	so it provides **no drift attribution** ΓÇö it validates the
430	instrumentation, not the calibration (consistent with Theorem 1; no
431	free lunch).
432	
433	---
434	
435	## 6. Estimator and compensation logic
436	
437	### 6.1 Estimator states and structure
438	
439	**Proposed** (structure per stage-20 estimator-requirements rows;
440	augmented-bias-state precedent [H015], [H004]):
441	
442	- **Core filter (always on):** states
443	  `x = [B, x_I, b_H, b_C (or m), ╧ä_L]`, with `S_H, K_C` held at their
444	  last anchored values between epochs; random-walk/OU priors band-limited
445	  below `╧ë_d`; innovation ╧ç┬▓ monitored per channel.
446	- **Gain-tracking layer (HA):** lock-in outputs `╧Ç_H, ╧Ç_C` as auxiliary
447	  measurements updating slowly-varying multiplicative states
448	  `s_H = S_H/S_H^anchor`, `k_C = K_C/K_C^anchor`; the filter treats them
449	  as direct (noisy) observations of the relative gains, valid under the
450	  ┬º5.2 orthogonality condition.
451	- **Anchor-epoch processors (scheduled):** vacuum-shot least squares on
452	  `[B_ref, 1]` and `[ß╕é_ref, 1]` (CASE D); zero-field offset reads
453	  (CASE C2); repeated-waveform ratio regression (CASE 6). Each epoch
454	  writes `{┼£_H, K╠é_C, b╠é_H, b╠é_C, ─£_cal, cov}` to the calibration ledger
455	  (S5) with full uncertainty.
456	- **Fault bank (always on):** ╧ü-jump alarm; triangle-closure residual;
457	  innovation ╧ç┬▓; GLR change-point tests on gain states;
458	  loss-of-injection detector; (top tier) three-channel voting per
459	  CASE G / confounding test 6. Abrupt-vs-slow signatures are used as a
460	  *heuristic prior* for failure-vs-drift sorting, never as proof
461	  (stage-20 confounding row 6).
462	- **Honesty constraint (binding):** in any regime where stage 20 proves
463	  non-identifiability (CASE A between anchors, CASE F quasi-static
464	  without injection), the estimator must **freeze** the corresponding
465	  states and inflate reported uncertainty, not "converge" on its prior
466	  (stage-20 ┬º5.3 warning). This is a required behavior, tested in the
467	  simulation plan (test T-NI).
468	
469	### 6.2 Four compensation modes (stage-required distinction)
470	
471	| Mode | Mechanism | Timing | What it corrects | Identifiability basis |
472	|---|---|---|---|---|
473	| **Online compensation** | core KF (integrator drift, offsets vs anchors); lock-in gain tracking; ╧ü-alarm-gated deweighting | continuous | `x_I, m, ╧ä_L, b_C`; relative `S_H, K_C` (HA); field estimate fusion | C02 direction (CASE C2/I); CASE E products; CASE A invariant |
474	| **Scheduled calibration** | vacuum-shot anchor; zero-field epochs; repeated-waveform ratios; bench recal at maintenance | per shot cycle / run day / vent | absolute `S_H, K_C, b_H, b_C, G_cal`; drift-ratio history | CASE D; CASE C2; CASE 6 |
475	| **Fault detection** | fault bank S4 (╧ç┬▓, ╧ü-jump, GLR, closure, loss-of-injection, voting) | continuous | nothing ΓÇö it *flags*; triggers deweighting, early anchor, or channel exclusion | detection Γëá attribution (confounding 6); attribution only with diversity (CASE G) |
476	| **Post-exposure correction** | reprocess archived raw data against the calibration ledger: piecewise `┼£_H(t)` between anchors interpolated with monotone-in-fluence constraint *only if* rung-5 data supports it; annealing-aware validity windows (C22 hysteresis) | offline, after campaign/exposure | historical field estimates; drift-curve reconstruction `S_H(╬ª)` | CASE 6 ratios + anchor epochs; interpolation model is labeled Inferred until rung-5 data exists |
477	
478	Post-exposure correction is where dosimetry earns its place: fluence from
479	foils (C26) time-bases the reconstruction; without species-matched
480	dosimetry the reconstruction cannot claim a dose axis at all (C16).
481	
482	### 6.3 Uncertainty propagation (Derived budgets)
483	
484	Every reported field value carries a variance composed of:
485	
486	1. **Anchor chain:** vacuum-model error `╬┤B_ref/B_ref` maps 1:1 into
487	   `╬┤S_H/S_H` (CASE D); position error via `ΓêçG┬╖╬┤r`; misalignment enters
488	   as `S_H┬╖cos╬╕_m` (inseparable single-axis ΓÇö budgeted, not estimated);
489	   current-log accuracy; timing skew into `ß╕é_ref`.
490	2. **Between-anchor drift:** random-walk growth of frozen states ΓÇö
491	   `var(S_H)` grows as `q_S┬╖(tΓêÆt_anchor)` with `q_S` set from measured
492	   drift statistics (bench Tier 1 first, updated by rung-5 data);
493	   reported, never hidden. This is where Theorem 1's common-mode
494	   blindness lives in the numbers.
495	3. **Gain-tracking noise:** lock-in variance (┬º5.2 formula) plus `G_cal`
496	   drift-rate allowance (┬º5.4.3).
497	4. **Coil-as-reference term (case 2 use):** coil-chain bias `╬┤(╬öB)`
498	   enters `╬┤S_H/S_H Γëê ΓêÆ╬┤(╬öB)/╬öB` multiplicatively; integrator noise
499	   makes coil-derived `╬öB` a random walk, bounding usable regression
500	   windows (stage-20 ┬º5.2).
501	5. **Environmental attribution:** temperature-coefficient uncertainty ├ù
502	   ╬öT excursion; TΓÇôD collinearity penalty when histories correlate
503	   (CASE J: attribution variance ΓåÆ Γê₧ as correlation ΓåÆ 1 ΓÇö reported as a
504	   conditioning number, not silently regularized).
505	6. **Dosimetry (campaign):** foil C/E = 1.05 ┬▒ 0.13 class uncertainty
506	   (C26) on the fluence axis; surrogate-to-target flux-gap factor stated
507	   whenever screening data is extrapolated ([R073], [R074]).
508	
509	Accuracy claims in this architecture are therefore always of the form
510	"X % relative to the anchor epoch, growing at the stated rate between
511	anchors" ΓÇö no unconditional absolute-accuracy number is claimable, by
512	Theorem 1 (Derived).
513	
514	---
515	
516	## 7. Radiation mechanisms: in-situ measurable vs ex-situ (stage-required)
517	
518	| Mechanism / quantity | In-situ measurable? | How / why not | Evidence |
519	|---|---|---|---|
520	| Relative Hall gain drift `S_H(t)/S_H(t_0)` | **Yes** (HA) | lock-in products; anchor ratios; repeated waveform | CASE E/6; C11 precedent [H059] |
521	| Absolute `S_H` | **Per-epoch only** | vacuum-shot anchor (machine off-plasma) | CASE D; [P013] |
522	| Hall offset drift `b_H` | **Per-epoch only** | zero-field epochs; structurally invisible to AC injection | Theorem 1; C07 |
523	| Hall resistance `R_H` (carrier removal / mobility proxy) | **Yes** | 4-wire bias telemetry; no field reference needed | Derived; mechanism per [R003], [R043] |
524	| Hall noise spectrum change | **Yes** | quiescent-period PSD monitoring | Derived (monitoring practice) |
525	| Coil/integrator additive drift (`b_C`, `m`, RIEMF) | **Yes** (given Hall anchor + dB/dt variation) | the C02 hardware-proven direction; zero-dB/dt segments read `b_C` directly | [H004], [H005], C19 |
526	| Coil gain `K_C` / effective-area drift | **Partially** | `╧Ç_C` product + anchor epochs; no in-situ separation of `A_eff` from readout gain | CASE E/D; gap: no dose-to-area data ([R069], [R070] note) |
527	| Which channel drifted (attribution) | **Only with diversity** | three-channel voting + measured T + decorrelated histories | CASE G/J; C18, C21 |
528	| Temperature-vs-dose split of a drift | **Conditionally** | measured T + pre-characterized `╬▒_S` + engineered decorrelation | CASE J; C22 hysteresis limit |
529	| Fluence/spectrum at the head | **Integrating in situ, read ex situ** | activation foils: retrieved and counted after exposure; online per-species spectrometry at the head is not in the evidence base (Unknown) | C26, [R072]ΓÇô[R076] |
530	| Mobility vs carrier-density decomposition of a gain drift | **No** | requires van der Pauw / Hall-bar lab measurement | [R003] method |
531	| Transmutation dopant identification | **No** | materials analysis (post-exposure) | [R025], [R001], C24 |
532	| Deep-level/trap characterization | **No** | DLTS-class lab work | radiation review ┬º1 |
533	| Annealing recovery curves | **No** (requires controlled T-history) | furnace/ramp protocols post-exposure | [R024], C22 |
534	| Insulation resistance / interlaminar integrity | **No** (dedicated test) | megger/mechanical test at maintenance | [R061], [R062], [R068] |
535	| Readout SET rate | **Yes** (detection) | fault bank catches ms-scale transients; correction is exclusion, not calibration | [R052], C25 |
536	
537	---
538	
539	## 8. Cross-sensitivity, common-mode failure, reference degradation
540	
541	- **Cross-axis response:** single-axis analysis assumed (stage-20 ┬º2.4);
542	  misalignment inseparable from gain with a single-axis reference ΓÇö
543	  budgeted (┬º6.3.1); bench characterization required (Tier 1);
544	  vertical-Hall cross-sensitivity evidence [H047].
545	- **Temperature cross-sensitivity:** first-class state; the J-corr
546	  failure (T Γê¥ D ΓåÆ rank 1) is a *scheduling* problem ΓÇö engineered thermal
547	  excursions decorrelated from fluence accumulation are part of the
548	  campaign design, not an afterthought (CASE J-decorr).
549	- **Common-mode failure classes and their only countermeasures:**
550	  (i) Hall+coil common gain shift ΓÇö invisible in-pair (Theorem 1);
551	  countered only by anchor cadence (C) and mechanism diversity (D);
552	  (ii) die+winding common shift ΓÇö invisible to self-test (C05);
553	  countered by the machine-model anchor;
554	  (iii) whole-head common environment (T excursion, flux transient) ΓÇö
555	  countered by telemetry (T, `R_H`) and post-hoc reprocessing;
556	  (iv) shared-electronics events (SETs, rail glitches) ΓÇö countered by
557	  fault bank + channel-level electrical separation (block design ┬º4.3).
558	- **Reference degradation:** every reference in this architecture is
559	  assigned a *degradation observable*: `G_cal` ΓåÆ closure + anchor solve
560	  (┬º5.4ΓÇô5.5); machine-current model ΓåÆ vacuum-shot residuals vs model
561	  ([P013]-class verification); metallic-Hall witness ΓåÆ its own `R` and
562	  noise telemetry + ratio consistency (single-source basis flagged,
563	  C18); zero-field epochs ΓåÆ ambient-field audit (risk RR-24); dosimetry
564	  ΓåÆ C/E protocol (C26). A reference with no degradation observable is
565	  not admitted into the estimator (design rule, Derived from stage-20
566	  ┬º4 feasibility-matrix reading).
567	
568	---
569	
570	## 9. Accuracy/cost drivers and budget tiers
571	
572	No vendor prices are quoted anywhere (none are in the evidence base);
573	cost classes are order-of-magnitude *labels* (labeled estimate) tied to
574	`DECISION_FRAMEWORK.md`'s tier structure. Stop/go gates G0ΓÇôG6 are defined
575	in the validation plan ┬º10 and summarized here.
576	
577	| Tier | Content | Dominant accuracy drivers | Dominant cost drivers | Entry gate | Exit (go) gate | Stop rule |
578	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
579	| **T0 ΓÇö simulation** | reusable package per validation plan; synthetic fault injection | model fidelity to ┬º2 parameterization; honesty test T-NI | engineering time only | ΓÇö | **G0:** estimator meets metric targets on identifiable scenarios AND correctly reports non-identifiability on CASE-A/F scenarios | if targets unreachable even with perfect references ΓåÆ redesign before any hardware spend |
580	| **T1 ΓÇö bench truth (MVD hardware)** | existing Hall + wound coil + precision current source/Helmholtz + temperature control; traceable transfer standard | reference traceability; temperature-coefficient characterization; noise floors; alignment | bench components; transfer-standard access; time | G0 pass | **G1:** anchored-hybrid calibration repeatable across ΓëÑ3 cycles within the T0-predicted uncertainty; `╬▒_S, ╬▓_b` characterized | if bench repeatability Γë½ prediction and cause not found ΓåÆ architecture assumptions wrong; halt and diagnose |
581	| **T2 ΓÇö self-test hybrid (HA hardware)** | + cal winding, traceable current ref, dual lock-in, drift emulation, long-duration soak | `G_cal` characterization; heating ceiling (┬º5.3); spectral survey quality; emulated-drift recovery accuracy | winding fabrication/characterization; reference electronics; long-run test time | G1 pass | **G2/G3:** emulated gain/offset drifts recovered within CI; closure residual stable over ΓëÑ multi-day soak; drift-attribution logic validated on emulated faults | if injected-reference stability cannot beat the drift resolution target ΓåÆ Option B layer is not earning its complexity; descope to MVD (C-only anchoring) |
582	| **T3 ΓÇö environmental qualification (collaborator-led)** | material screening ΓåÆ neutron/gamma qualification with dosimetry, material diversity, pre/post + in-situ protocol per FOCS/foil templates (C20/C26) | species/spectrum match to target environment (C12/C16); dosimetry C/E; sample size; T control during exposure | facility access (never assumed ΓÇö no facility commitment exists in this plan); collaborator effort; activated-hardware logistics | G3 pass + collaborator agreement | **G4/G5:** screening quantifies `f_S,s` with stated uncertainty; qualification confirms compensation closes the loop at target accuracy | if screening shows drift below the in-situ method's detection floor ΓåÆ in-situ recal is unnecessary (simplify to MVD + scheduled recal: a *good* outcome); if drift is large, non-monotonic, and unattributable ΓåÆ hybrid compensation is falsified for that material; pivot to Option D/F material change |
583	
584	(Four tiers ΓëÑ the required three; T0 costs no hardware and is the
585	mandatory first spend.)
586	
587	### 9.4 HSX-paper decoupling (binding statement)
588	
589	Tiers T0ΓÇôT2 and gates G0ΓÇôG3 involve **no radiation exposure of any
590	kind** and constitute the complete architecture-validation content
591	relevant to the user's current first-author HSX trajectory. T3 exists
592	only as a collaborator-led, later or coauthored work package
593	(per `MISSION.md` boundary and root scope rule); no output of T0ΓÇôT2, and
594	no HSX deliverable, depends on T3 occurring. Radiation results may be
595	*cited as complementary or outlook* in first-author work, never claimed
596	experimentally (root `CLAUDE.md` scope rule).
597	
598	---
599	
600	## 10. Unresolved engineering risks (summary)
601	
602	Full register with likelihood/impact/mitigation:
603	`outputs\03_RADIATION_RISK_REGISTER.csv` (24 rows, RR-01ΓÇªRR-24). The five
604	that most threaten the architecture (Derived ranking by
605	impact ├ù irreducibility):
606	
607	1. **RR-01/RR-02 ΓÇö GaN drift magnitude unknown (C14):** every cadence,
608	   window, and threshold in ┬º5ΓÇô6 is sized provisionally until rung-5
609	   screening data exists; the architecture is designed to *measure* its
610	   way out of this, but cannot be proven sufficient before that data.
611	2. **RR-13 ΓÇö common-mode blindness between anchors (Theorem 1):**
612	   irreducible in-pair; bounded only by anchor cadence and (top tier)
613	   diversity; the residual is an honest uncertainty term, not a solved

615	3. **RR-12/RR-08 ΓÇö reference-chain drift under radiation (`G_cal`,
616	   `A_eff`):** zero direct evidence either way (no dose-to-geometry
617	   measurements exist); triangulation bounds but does not eliminate it.
618	4. **RR-18 ΓÇö witness-channel single-source basis ([R071], C18):** the
619	   attribution tier rests on an unreplicated null result.
620	5. **RR-16/RR-17 ΓÇö planning-level extrapolation traps (C16, C17):** any
621	   shortcut that sizes the design from proton or single-species data
622	   risks the documented ~14├ù class of error; enforced by the
623	   species-indexing discipline of ┬º2.

626	
627	## 11. Consistency statement
628	
629	Checked line-by-line against stage 20: every "covers" claim in ┬º3ΓÇô┬º7
630	cites the enabling CASE and inherits its conditions; no claim exceeds the
631	feasibility matrix (`02_MUTUAL_CALIBRATION_FEASIBILITY.md` ┬º2); the
632	estimator is required to refuse convergence where stage 20 proves

# 03 ΓÇö Radiation compensation architecture

Stage 30 (`30_radiation_compensation`). Produced and signed off by Fable 5
(xhigh). Source IDs (`Hxxx`, `Rxxx`, `Pxxx`) refer to
`outputs\01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv`; claim IDs (`Cxx`) refer to
`outputs\01_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv`. Stage-20 citations (`┬ºx`, `CASE x`) refer to
`outputs\02_OBSERVABILITY_AND_IDENTIFIABILITY.md` and
`outputs\02_MUTUAL_CALIBRATION_FEASIBILITY.md`. Labels: **Observed /
Derived / Inferred / Proposed / Unknown** per `CLAUDE.md`.

**Scope discipline (binding, from `00_CONFLICT_LEDGER.md` C6 and
`MISSION.md`):** everything in this file is a *specification* of what an
architecture and its validation would require. Nothing here commits the
user's current first-author HSX work to any radiation experiment; all
irradiation content is written for a later, coauthored, or collaborator-led
work package. Radiation testing is **not** a prerequisite for any HSX
deliverable in this plan (see ┬º9.4 and the validation plan ┬º10).

---

## 1. Design problem, inherited constraints

Stage 20 fixed the ground rules the architecture must respect (all Derived
there, restated for use):

1. **Theorem 1 (two-parameter gauge group):** an unreferenced Hall+coil
   pair can never identify absolute scale or Hall offset; common-mode gain
   drift is observationally identical to a field change (┬º3, CASE A).
2. **Direction asymmetry:** HallΓåÆcoil correction is hardware-proven
   ([H004], [H005], [P003]; claim C02); coilΓåÆHall works for **gain only**,
   conditionally (trusted coil chain + ╬öB excitation, CASE B; single
   non-fusion precedent [H059], C11), and **never for offset**.
3. **Quasi-static blindness:** during flat-top/steady field the pair alone
   provides nothing (CASE F); all calibration value there comes from
   engineered anchors (C04 analog).
4. **Attribution requires diversity:** with everything drifting, detection
   (╧ü = S_H/K_C alarm) survives but attribution does not; a third,
   mechanism-diverse channel or an absolute anchor is required (CASE G,
   confounding tests 2 and 6).
5. **Radiation magnitudes for the user's device family are Unknown:** no
   GaN/AlGaN Hall-plate neutron dataset exists (C14); cross-species
   scaling can err ~14├ù (C16, [R042]); mixed fields are non-additive (C17).
   The architecture must therefore *measure* drift, not assume a model of
   it, and must treat every drift-magnitude number as a parameter to be
   determined by the validation ladder ΓÇö never as an input taken from
   evidence that does not exist.

The design question is therefore **not** "can the pair self-calibrate"
(answered: no, ┬º3) but **"which minimal set of anchors, references, and
diversity keeps every drift parameter of interest observable at the target
accuracy, at each budget level."** (Derived framing.)

## 2. Parameterization

### 2.1 Hall channel

```text
y_H(t) = S_H(t) ┬╖ [B(t) + B_inj(t)] + b_H(t) + n_H(t)
```

with the drift decomposition (Derived structure; magnitudes per-term
Observed/Unknown as flagged):

```text
S_H(t) = S_H0 ┬╖ [ 1 + ╬▒_S┬╖(T(t)ΓêÆT0) + f_S,s(╬ª_s(t), ╧å╠ç_s, T_irr) + h_S(a(t)) ]
b_H(t) = b_H0 + ╬▓_b┬╖(T(t)ΓêÆT0) + f_b,s(╬ª_s(t), ΓÇª) + h_b(a(t)) + w_b(t)
```

- `S_H0` [V/T at fixed bias]: bench-calibrated initial sensitivity;
  absolute value only ever from an external anchor (┬º3, Theorem 1).
- `╬▒_S` [1/K]: temperature coefficient, pre-characterized on the bench
  (Tier 1); required input for confounding test 5 (CASE J).
- `f_S,s(╬ª_s)` : radiation-induced gain drift as a function of fluence
  `╬ª_s` **indexed by species/spectrum s** (thermal-inclusive fission,
  fast-fission, 14 MeV D-T, gamma, proton kept strictly separate ΓÇö
  `SOURCE_POLICY.md` discipline). Observed for InSb: spectrum-dependent,
  transmutation-attributed under thermal-inclusive spectra ([R001],
  [R002], C12) and mobility ΓêÆ75ΓÇªΓêÆ90 % at 6.6ΓÇô7.0e17 fast n/cm┬▓ ([R003],
  C13). **Unknown for GaN/AlGaN Hall plates under any neutron spectrum**
  (C14); proton data on AlGaN/GaN micro-Hall sensors exists ([R012],
  [R013], [R015], C15) but must not be scaled across species (C16).
- `h_S(a)` : annealing/recovery term with hysteresis state `a(t)`
  (temperature-history functional). Observed for GaN-family TID: two-regime
  behavior, partial recovery at 200 ┬░C/25 min ([R024], [R033], C22);
  partial anneal recovery of proton-degraded micro-Hall sensors ([R012],
  C15). Transmutation contributions are **non-annealable at service
  temperature** ([R025], [R001], C24) ΓÇö `h_S` recovers only the
  displacement/ionization share.
- `b_H0, w_b` : residual offset floor and its random walk. Current
  spinning reduces but does not eliminate offset ([H034], [H035], C07),
  so `b_H` stays a free state in every estimator here.
- `R_H(t)` [╬⌐]: device input/output resistance. Carrier removal and
  mobility loss raise it (Observed for irradiated Hall materials, [R003],
  [R043]); it sets thermal noise `╧â_H┬▓ Γê¥ 4kT┬╖R_out┬╖╬öf` and shifts the
  bias operating point. **`R_H` is cheaply measurable in situ** (known
  bias current, measured voltage drop) and is carried as an auxiliary
  monitored output ΓÇö a drift *witness* that requires no field reference
  at all (Derived; see ┬º7).
- `n_H` : noise, variance `╧â_H┬▓`; 1/f knee and EMI live in the drift band
  (stage-20 ┬º2.5 convention). Radiation-induced noise increase is a
  monitorable in-situ quantity (┬º7).
- Bias state during exposure matters and is recorded as a condition
  (Observed as reporting requirement, `SOURCE_POLICY.md`; bias-state
  dependence documented for packaged ICs [R011], [R018], [R019]).

### 2.2 Coil channel

```text
y_C(t) = K_C(t) ┬╖ (h_C Γêù d[B+B_inj]/dt)(t) + b_C(t) + n_C(t)     (direct)
dx_I/dt = ΓêÆx_I/╧ä_L + g┬╖dB/dt + m(t),  y_I = x_I + n_I            (integrated)
```

## 4. Recommended architectures

### 4.1 Minimum viable design ΓÇö MVD "anchored hybrid" (Options A+C+zero-field epochs)

**Proposed.** For the user's machine context (a pulsed stellarator with
logged coil currents, e-beam-validated vacuum fields [P013], and
between-shot zero-field access):

- **Hardware:** existing GaN Hall channel (current-spun) + one wound/PCB
  coil on the same axis + co-located temperature sensor + shared,
  time-synchronized DAQ. No new in-vessel actuator.
- **References:** (i) vacuum-shot machine-current anchor (CASE D: all
  four parameters, per anchor epoch; requires ΓëÑ2 field levels and a
  ramp+flat-top so dB/dt takes ΓëÑ2 values ΓÇö the CASE I-ramp condition);
  (ii) pre/post-shot zero-field epochs for `b_H`, `b_C` (CASE C2, full
  rank; requires remanent/ambient field controlled or measured ΓÇö
  assumption flagged, risk RR-24); (iii) an initial bench absolute
  calibration traceable to an NMR-class or equivalent transfer standard
  ([H041], [H042], [H064]).
- **Estimator:** augmented-state Kalman filter with random-walk bias
  states (the C02 direction for integrator drift; structure per stage-20
  CASE1 row of `02_ESTIMATOR_REQUIREMENTS.csv`), plus per-epoch linear
  regressions at anchors, plus the continuous ╧ü-alarm.
- **What it delivers:** full parameter set re-anchored every vacuum-shot
  epoch; offsets every shot cycle; continuous differential-drift
  detection between anchors. **What it cannot do:** attribute drift
  between anchor epochs, or see common-mode drift between anchors
  (Theorem 1) ΓÇö accepted at this tier and stated in the uncertainty
  budget (┬º6.3).

### 4.2 Higher-accuracy design ΓÇö HA "triangulated self-test hybrid" (H = A+B+C+E, + D at top tier)

**Proposed.** Adds to the MVD:

- **Embedded calibration winding** around/adjacent to the Hall die with a
  traceable current source, spectrally-orthogonal (or toggled) injection,
  and digital lock-in demodulation on **both** channels (┬º5). Delivers
  continuous relative gain tracking `S_H(t)┬╖G_cal(t)` and
  `K_C(t)┬╖G_cal(t)` ΓÇö including through quasi-static periods where the
  MVD is blind (CASE F remedy).
- **Repeated-reference-waveform tracking** (Option E, CASE 6 algebra):
  every standard vacuum ramp is regressed against the shot-0 epoch,
  yielding gain-drift ratios with the machine as the (verified-
  reproducibility) excitation source.
- **Top tier only ΓÇö material-diverse witness channel** (Option D): a
  metallic-Hall (or otherwise mechanism-diverse) die beside the GaN die,
  enabling three-channel voting and differential radiation attribution
  (CASE G + CASE J conditions: measured T, pre-characterized
  coefficients, decorrelated T/D histories). Explicitly contingent on
  replicating [R071]'s single-source null result during the validation
  ladder (risk RR-18).
- **Dosimetry interface (campaign contexts only):** provision for
  co-located activation foils per the validated two-step protocol (C26).

  commitment (┬º9.4).

## 5. Embedded calibration winding ΓÇö required analysis

**The stage question: can the winding's field isolate Hall gain and bias
in the presence of an unknown ambient field?**

### 5.1 What injection can and cannot isolate (Derived; CASE E)

With `B_inj(t) = G_cal┬╖I_cal(t)` spectrally orthogonal to ambient
content:

- **Gain: yes, as a product.** Lock-in demodulation of `y_H` at the
  injection frequency estimates `S_H┬╖G_cal` (CASE E, rank 6/7 ΓÇö both
  gain functions identifiable). Relative gain tracking
  `[S_H┬╖G_cal](t) / [S_H┬╖G_cal](t_0)` is the radiation-monitoring
  quantity of interest and is insensitive to the ambient field entirely.
- **Bias: no ΓÇö structurally.** The DC null survives every AC injection
  (CASE E): a Hall offset is observationally identical to a static
  ambient shift. Toggled DC injection (`┬▒I_cal,DC`, difference of
  states) measures *gain at the DC operating point* ΓÇö the difference
  `╬öy_H = 2┬╖S_H┬╖G_cal┬╖I_cal,DC` cancels both `b_H` and static ambient ΓÇö
  but never `b_H` itself. Offset requires zero-field/known-field epochs
  (MVD anchor ii) or an absolute reference. **Any design document
  claiming an embedded winding "calibrates the offset" is wrong**
  (Derived, Theorem 1 ╬▓-direction).
- Ambient variation *during* a toggle period leaks into the toggle
  difference; mitigation is fast square-wave toggling with synchronous
  demod, with the main coil as a dB/dt witness to gate/correct toggle
  epochs (Derived).

### 5.2 Frequency plan and lock-in detection (Derived design rules)

- Place `f_inj` in the **overlap band**: above the drift band `╧ë_d`,
  below the Hall pole, inside the coil's flat response ΓÇö
  `╧ë_d < 2╧Ç┬╖f_inj < min(a_Hall, ╧ë_C,max)` ΓÇö and in a measured-quiet
  region of the ambient spectrum. Spectral collision with ambient
  content re-creates the rank deficiency (CASE E-collide: 5/7) ΓÇö this is
  a hard requirement, not a preference. Machine EMI lines (power
  supplies, spinning-current harmonics) must be surveyed first
  (Hall-sensor EMI susceptibility is documented in adjacent contexts,
  [P021], [P022], C30).
- Coding (PRBS or slow frequency hopping) or on/off toggling makes the
  orthogonality verifiable: the estimator checks that the demodulated
  output tracks the injection schedule (loss-of-injection and
  collision-detection test in fault bank S4).
- Lock-in variance (first-order, matched-filter): for a sine injection
  of amplitude `B_a = G_cal┬╖I_a`,
  `var(┼£_H┬╖G_cal) Γëê 2╧â_H┬▓ / (T_int ┬╖ I_a┬▓┬╖G_cal┬▓)` ΓÇö integration time
  `T_int` trades against the drift timescale being tracked
  (quasi-stationarity window, stage-20 assumption 3). Choose `T_int` Γë¬
  expected drift correlation time; since GaN drift magnitudes are
  Unknown (C14), `T_int` is a *scheduled parameter*, revisited after
  validation rung 5 data exists.
- Coil-side lock-in: the coil sees `d(B_inj)/dt`, amplitude
  `Γê¥ ╧ë_inj┬╖B_a`, so coil-side SNR *improves* with frequency ΓÇö favoring
  the upper part of the allowed band, jointly optimized against the Hall
  pole margin (case 9: injecting near the pole additionally identifies
  Hall dynamics; CASE H-broad).

### 5.3 Amplitude, heating, EMI (Derived design constraints)

- **Amplitude floor:** `B_a` must give usable lock-in SNR within `T_int`
  (formula above) at the Hall noise floor.
- **Heating ceiling (self-interference):** winding dissipation
  `P_cal = I_rms┬▓┬╖R_cal` raises die temperature by `╬öT_die = R_th┬╖P_cal`,
  which enters the very term (`╬▒_S┬╖╬öT`) the system is trying to
  monitor. Self-consistency condition:
  `|╬▒_S| ┬╖ R_th ┬╖ R_cal ┬╖ I_rms┬▓ Γë¬ ╬┤_S` (target relative-gain
  resolution). This couples winding resistance, thermal design, and
  amplitude; it is a bench-characterizable inequality (Tier 1), and a
  reason the winding cannot simply be driven harder to buy SNR.
- **EMI/coupling:** the injection tone couples into the main coil by
  mutual inductance ΓÇö this is *used* (┬º5.5), but also contaminates the
  coil's field measurement at `f_inj`; the demodulator must notch the
  injection line out of the field-estimation path. Injection leads must
  be twisted/guarded so the *cable*, not just the winding, does not
  radiate (RIEMF and pickup discipline as for the main coil, C19).
- Under radiation, the cal circuit itself is exposed: RIEMF adds an
  error current/EMF in the injection loop ([R056] mechanism; Inferred
  transfer ΓÇö flagged, risk RR-12), and insulation leakage changes the
  delivered `I_cal` unless the readback shunt sits electrically close to
  the winding (design rule: **sense at the winding, not at the source**).

### 5.4 The winding's own reference problem (stage-required; Derived)

`G_cal` is geometry + magnetics. The stage forbids assuming it stays
known, and the evidence supports the caution: **no measurement of
radiation-induced coil-constant/effective-area drift exists for any
coil** (radiation review ┬º4 gap; metrology baseline [R069], [R070]), and
thermal expansion alone changes `G_cal` at the `╬▒_thermal┬╖╬öT` level.
Consequences:

1. Only the **products** `S_H┬╖G_cal`, `K_C┬╖G_cal` are identifiable
   (CASE E). A reference-chain drift is indistinguishable from sensor
   gain drift *within the winding system alone*.
2. The JET RHP record shows the strength and the limit of the same-die
   approach: 11.5 years, SD Γëê 0.07 % sensitivity stability across
   >19,000 pulses including D-T ([H003], [H007], C05) ΓÇö but a co-located
   same-technology reference cannot by construction detect common-mode
   (shared radiation/thermal) drift of die and winding together (C05
   limitation). Mechanism diversity (geometric constant vs semiconductor
   transport) makes common-mode drift *physically unlikely* but not
   logically excluded (Inferred, stage-20 ┬º5.5).
3. **Resolution in this architecture: triangulation, not trust.** The
   winding is itself referenced against the machine-model anchor at
   every vacuum-shot epoch (CASE D identifies `S_H` and `K_C`
   absolutely; combined with the lock-in products this *solves for
   `G_cal` at each anchor epoch* ΓÇö Derived). Between anchors, `G_cal`
   drift is bounded by the closure test below, and its residual drift
   rate enters the uncertainty budget explicitly (┬º6.3) rather than
   being assumed zero.

### 5.5 Triangle-closure consistency test (Derived; added design feature)

The three continuously-available quantities

```text
╧ü_HC   = S_H/K_C            (ambient AC cross-regression, CASE A invariant)
╧Ç_H    = S_H┬╖G_cal          (Hall-side lock-in)
╧Ç_C    = K_C┬╖G_cal          (coil-side lock-in)
```

satisfy the identity `╧Ç_H / ╧Ç_C Γëí ╧ü_HC` for all t. The **closure
residual** `╬╡_╬ö = ╧Ç_H/╧Ç_C ΓêÆ ╧ü_HC` is measurable continuously and must be
zero to within noise regardless of drift in any single quantity.
`╬╡_╬ö Γëá 0` indicts the *measurement paths* (demodulator fault, spectral
collision, coil nonlinearity at `f_inj`, injection-line contamination) ΓÇö
a fault-detection channel that costs nothing extra. Note what it cannot
do: closure holds identically under any {`S_H`, `K_C`, `G_cal`} drift,
so it provides **no drift attribution** ΓÇö it validates the
instrumentation, not the calibration (consistent with Theorem 1; no
free lunch).

---

## 6. Estimator and compensation logic

### 6.1 Estimator states and structure

**Proposed** (structure per stage-20 estimator-requirements rows;
augmented-bias-state precedent [H015], [H004]):

- **Core filter (always on):** states
  `x = [B, x_I, b_H, b_C (or m), ╧ä_L]`, with `S_H, K_C` held at their
  last anchored values between epochs; random-walk/OU priors band-limited
  below `╧ë_d`; innovation ╧ç┬▓ monitored per channel.
- **Gain-tracking layer (HA):** lock-in outputs `╧Ç_H, ╧Ç_C` as auxiliary
  measurements updating slowly-varying multiplicative states
  `s_H = S_H/S_H^anchor`, `k_C = K_C/K_C^anchor`; the filter treats them
  as direct (noisy) observations of the relative gains, valid under the
  ┬º5.2 orthogonality condition.
- **Anchor-epoch processors (scheduled):** vacuum-shot least squares on
  `[B_ref, 1]` and `[ß╕é_ref, 1]` (CASE D); zero-field offset reads
  (CASE C2); repeated-waveform ratio regression (CASE 6). Each epoch
  writes `{┼£_H, K╠é_C, b╠é_H, b╠é_C, ─£_cal, cov}` to the calibration ledger
  (S5) with full uncertainty.
- **Fault bank (always on):** ╧ü-jump alarm; triangle-closure residual;
  innovation ╧ç┬▓; GLR change-point tests on gain states;
  loss-of-injection detector; (top tier) three-channel voting per
  CASE G / confounding test 6. Abrupt-vs-slow signatures are used as a
  *heuristic prior* for failure-vs-drift sorting, never as proof
  (stage-20 confounding row 6).
- **Honesty constraint (binding):** in any regime where stage 20 proves
  non-identifiability (CASE A between anchors, CASE F quasi-static
  without injection), the estimator must **freeze** the corresponding
  states and inflate reported uncertainty, not "converge" on its prior
  (stage-20 ┬º5.3 warning). This is a required behavior, tested in the
  simulation plan (test T-NI).

### 6.2 Four compensation modes (stage-required distinction)

| Mode | Mechanism | Timing | What it corrects | Identifiability basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Online compensation** | core KF (integrator drift, offsets vs anchors); lock-in gain tracking; ╧ü-alarm-gated deweighting | continuous | `x_I, m, ╧ä_L, b_C`; relative `S_H, K_C` (HA); field estimate fusion | C02 direction (CASE C2/I); CASE E products; CASE A invariant |
| **Scheduled calibration** | vacuum-shot anchor; zero-field epochs; repeated-waveform ratios; bench recal at maintenance | per shot cycle / run day / vent | absolute `S_H, K_C, b_H, b_C, G_cal`; drift-ratio history | CASE D; CASE C2; CASE 6 |
| **Fault detection** | fault bank S4 (╧ç┬▓, ╧ü-jump, GLR, closure, loss-of-injection, voting) | continuous | nothing ΓÇö it *flags*; triggers deweighting, early anchor, or channel exclusion | detection Γëá attribution (confounding 6); attribution only with diversity (CASE G) |
| **Post-exposure correction** | reprocess archived raw data against the calibration ledger: piecewise `┼£_H(t)` between anchors interpolated with monotone-in-fluence constraint *only if* rung-5 data supports it; annealing-aware validity windows (C22 hysteresis) | offline, after campaign/exposure | historical field estimates; drift-curve reconstruction `S_H(╬ª)` | CASE 6 ratios + anchor epochs; interpolation model is labeled Inferred until rung-5 data exists |

Post-exposure correction is where dosimetry earns its place: fluence from
foils (C26) time-bases the reconstruction; without species-matched
dosimetry the reconstruction cannot claim a dose axis at all (C16).

### 6.3 Uncertainty propagation (Derived budgets)

Every reported field value carries a variance composed of:

1. **Anchor chain:** vacuum-model error `╬┤B_ref/B_ref` maps 1:1 into
   `╬┤S_H/S_H` (CASE D); position error via `ΓêçG┬╖╬┤r`; misalignment enters
   as `S_H┬╖cos╬╕_m` (inseparable single-axis ΓÇö budgeted, not estimated);
   current-log accuracy; timing skew into `ß╕é_ref`.
2. **Between-anchor drift:** random-walk growth of frozen states ΓÇö
   `var(S_H)` grows as `q_S┬╖(tΓêÆt_anchor)` with `q_S` set from measured
   drift statistics (bench Tier 1 first, updated by rung-5 data);
   reported, never hidden. This is where Theorem 1's common-mode
   blindness lives in the numbers.
3. **Gain-tracking noise:** lock-in variance (┬º5.2 formula) plus `G_cal`
   drift-rate allowance (┬º5.4.3).
4. **Coil-as-reference term (case 2 use):** coil-chain bias `╬┤(╬öB)`
   enters `╬┤S_H/S_H Γëê ΓêÆ╬┤(╬öB)/╬öB` multiplicatively; integrator noise
   makes coil-derived `╬öB` a random walk, bounding usable regression
   windows (stage-20 ┬º5.2).
5. **Environmental attribution:** temperature-coefficient uncertainty ├ù
   ╬öT excursion; TΓÇôD collinearity penalty when histories correlate
   (CASE J: attribution variance ΓåÆ Γê₧ as correlation ΓåÆ 1 ΓÇö reported as a
   conditioning number, not silently regularized).
6. **Dosimetry (campaign):** foil C/E = 1.05 ┬▒ 0.13 class uncertainty
   (C26) on the fluence axis; surrogate-to-target flux-gap factor stated
   whenever screening data is extrapolated ([R073], [R074]).

Accuracy claims in this architecture are therefore always of the form
"X % relative to the anchor epoch, growing at the stated rate between
anchors" ΓÇö no unconditional absolute-accuracy number is claimable, by
Theorem 1 (Derived).

## 8. Cross-sensitivity, common-mode failure, reference degradation

- **Cross-axis response:** single-axis analysis assumed (stage-20 ┬º2.4);
  misalignment inseparable from gain with a single-axis reference ΓÇö
  budgeted (┬º6.3.1); bench characterization required (Tier 1);
  vertical-Hall cross-sensitivity evidence [H047].
- **Temperature cross-sensitivity:** first-class state; the J-corr
  failure (T Γê¥ D ΓåÆ rank 1) is a *scheduling* problem ΓÇö engineered thermal
  excursions decorrelated from fluence accumulation are part of the
  campaign design, not an afterthought (CASE J-decorr).
- **Common-mode failure classes and their only countermeasures:**
  (i) Hall+coil common gain shift ΓÇö invisible in-pair (Theorem 1);
  countered only by anchor cadence (C) and mechanism diversity (D);
  (ii) die+winding common shift ΓÇö invisible to self-test (C05);
  countered by the machine-model anchor;
  (iii) whole-head common environment (T excursion, flux transient) ΓÇö
  countered by telemetry (T, `R_H`) and post-hoc reprocessing;
  (iv) shared-electronics events (SETs, rail glitches) ΓÇö countered by
  fault bank + channel-level electrical separation (block design ┬º4.3).
- **Reference degradation:** every reference in this architecture is
  assigned a *degradation observable*: `G_cal` ΓåÆ closure + anchor solve

No vendor prices are quoted anywhere (none are in the evidence base);
cost classes are order-of-magnitude *labels* (labeled estimate) tied to

1	# Mission
2	
3	Produce a defensible research decision packageΓÇönot a sales pitchΓÇöfor a
4	Hall-effect plus inductive-coil magnetic diagnostic that may need to operate
5	under neutron, gamma, thermal, electromagnetic, and long-duration drift
6	stresses.
7	
8	The mission starts from the user's working hypothesis:
9	
10	> Validate and measure the Hall device first; add an inductive coil as a
11	> complementary hybrid; then provide a reusable module and simulation package.
12	
13	Treat that as a hypothesis to test. Do not make the conclusion fit it.
14	
15	The most important technical question is structural identifiability. A coil
16	measures field change while a Hall device measures field with unknown
17	sensitivity and bias. Redundancy does not automatically reveal which device
18	drifted. The analysis must explicitly determine when the combined system can
19	estimate field, Hall gain, Hall bias, coil gain/effective area, and integrator
20	drift, and when those quantities remain confounded.
21	
22	## Scope
23	
24	- Additional peer-reviewed literature beyond folder `06`.
25	- Direct and enabling evidence on radiation effects in Hall materials,
26	  contacts, biasing, packaging, readout electronics, cables, coils, and
27	  integrators.
28	- Observer/state-estimator design requirements and calibration references.
29	- Simulation and staged validation plan, including synthetic fault injection.
30	- Application and collaborator prioritization.
31	- Limitations and comparison against credible alternatives.
32	- Accuracy-versus-budget options and go/no-go gates.
33	
34	## Boundary conditions
35	
36	- Folder `06` and all other siblings are read-only context.
37	- Write only in this folder.
38	- Do not claim that the user has performed neutron or gamma experiments.
39	- The user's current first-author HSX work does not automatically acquire a
40	  radiation-test requirement. Radiation can remain a later, coauthored, or
41	  collaborator-led work package if the evidence supports that boundary.
42	- Do not contact any group, submit anything, or alter external resources.
43	- No geographic or affiliation exclusion applies to scientific sources.
44	  Evaluate evidence on quality and relevance.
45	- Do not confuse radiation species, spectrum, dose, fluence, dose rate,
46	  temperature, annealing, or device technology.
47	
48	## Success
49	
50	The package succeeds only if a skeptical advisor can trace each major claim,
51	see the failure cases, understand what the coil can and cannot calibrate, and
52	decide the next experiment without relying on undocumented model intuition.
53

1	# Source policy
2	
3	## Final ledger schema
4	
5	Every evidence-lane and final ledger CSV uses this exact header:
6	
7	```text
8	source_id,citation,title,authors,year,venue,doi,url,source_type,peer_review_status,quality_tier,topic_tags,claims_supported,verification_basis,access_level,notes

18	
19	Allowed quality tiers for verified papers:
20	
21	- `A`: high-quality original evidence, authoritative review, or strong
22	  high-impact/field-leading work directly relevant to a decision.
23	- `B`: sound peer-reviewed work with useful direct or enabling relevance.
24	- `C`: peer-reviewed contextual or narrow evidence that is helpful but less

39	- Radiation lane: at least 45.
40	- Applications/alternatives lane: at least 40.
41	- Final ledger: at least 120 after cross-lane deduplication.
42	- Final new-source delta: at least 75 relative to normalized DOI/title entries
43	  in folder `06\outputs\01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv`.
44	- Final topic quotas:
45	  - hybrid/coil/integrator/sensor fusion: 25
46	  - radiation/irradiation: 30
47	  - applications/alternatives: 25
48	  - calibration/observability/uncertainty: 20
49	
50	A source can satisfy multiple topic quotas. It counts only once toward 120.
51

53	
54	1. Original peer-reviewed journal or conference paper.
55	2. Official publisher metadata/full text.
56	3. DOI/Crossref or institutional repository metadata.
57	4. Standards and official facility documents for requirements/context.
58	5. Review articles for mapping and terminology.

1	# Decision framework
2	
3	## Central calibration question
4	
5	Use an explicit state/parameter model. A minimal starting point is:
6	
7	```text
8	y_H = S_H B + b_H + n_H
9	y_C = K_C dB/dt + b_C + n_C
10	```
11	
12	The architecture is not accepted merely because one channel measures DC and
13	the other measures AC. Determine the rank/observability or structural
14	identifiability of the augmented state under each scenario.
15	
16	| Scenario | Unknowns to test | Candidate reference |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| Bench calibration | field, Hall gain/bias, coil gain/offset | traceable magnet/NMR/fluxgate, calibrated current |
19	| Non-radiation machine operation | field, temperature drift, integrator drift | machine-current field model, repeatable shots |
20	| Radiation exposure | Hall gain/bias evolution, readout drift, temperature, field | embedded calibration coil, dosimetry, material-diverse reference |
21	| Long pulse | DC field and slow drift, coil integration constant | Hall/metal Hall reference, known excitation segments |
22	| Fast transient | bandwidth, phase, saturation, cross-axis effects | calibrated pulsed field/current waveform |
23	
24	For each scenario, state:
25	
26	- observable states/parameters;
27	- unobservable or confounded states/parameters;
28	- excitation/persistence requirements;
29	- prior/model assumptions;
30	- reference accuracy and traceability;
31	- estimator and uncertainty method;
32	- failure detector and fallback behavior.
33	
34	## Research-direction scoring
35	
36	Score each application from 0ΓÇô5 with evidence and uncertainty:
37

Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) leads a team that is testing plasma-jet driven magneto-inertial fusion (PJMIF), an innovative approach to controlled fusion energy production. The Plasma Liner Experiment (PLX) at Los Alamos National Laboratory serves as a critical testbed for investigating the feasibility of PJMIF. PLX is currently at Technology Readiness Level 3 with patents pending, and demonstrated milestones include operation of a 36-gun array to form spherical plasma liners.

## Program Support

The PJMIF approach has been selected for development under the ARPA-E ALPHA program.

## Error Field Measurement and Correction

The measurement and correction of error fields in Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) is critical to long pulse high beta operation, as small error fields may cause overloading of divertor plates in some configurations. The detection and correction of error fields on the W7-X experiment has been performed using the trim coil system in conjunction with the flux surface mapping diagnostic and high resolution infrared camera.

## Trim Coil System Function

Five additional normal conducting trim coils were designed to allow fine tuning of the main magnetic field during plasma operation. Small deviations from the ideal shape and position of the coils along with other influences like the presence of minor quantities of ferromagnetic material or the unavoidable deformation of the support structures during operation will result in magnetic field errors, especially errors which break the fivefold symmetry of the W7-X lead to additional magnetic islands and asymmetric loads on the divertor.

## Implementation at IPP Greifswald

I found relevant information about CERN's magnetic measurements capabilities. Here are the key results:

## CERN TE-MSC Magnetic Measurements Group

The CERN magnetic measurements group uses rotating coils, which analyze the flux intercepted by rotating a coil inside the magnet aperture to provide information about the strength, direction and quality of the field.

## Measurement Techniques

The CERN standard test magnet system uses the rotating coil method on superconducting dipoles of the Large Hadron Collider. Additionally, Hall probes have been used to map the magnetic field within, between, and around accelerator magnets, with CERN/NIKHEF Hall probes and specialized electronic readout systems employed for magnetic field measurements.

## Capabilities

The Hall probes are calibrated by CERN to a precision of one part in 10,000 with spherical harmonic coefficients that correct for small nonorthogonality of the Hall elements. Rotating coils facilitate the measurement of longitudinally integrated field integrals and transverse dependence of vertical and horizontal field integrals, and they are more accurate than Hall probes for determining field integrals.

The official CERN TE-MSC Magnetic Measurements group website (te-msc-mm.web.cern.ch) provides further details about their mission and measurement techniques for accelerator magnets.

## Overview

The P-24 Plasma Physics Group is located at Los Alamos National Laboratory in Los Alamos, NM, at MS-E526.

## Research Focus

The P-24 group conducts diverse plasma research including:

- Magnetized target fusion (MTF), Reconnection Scaling Experiment (RSX), laser driven shocks, radiological/chemical/biological decontamination using atmospheric pressure plasmas, fast gated X-ray cameras, and high energy density plasmas

- P-24 leads Los Alamos development of plasma processing with dual-benefit industrial applications

## Wendelstein 7-X Magnetic Diagnostics

An arrangement of magnetic sensors has been installed at the stellarator Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) including over 300 individual 3D shaped sensors like diamagnetic loops, Rogowski, Saddle and Mirnov coils.

### Rogowski Coils and Current Measurement

The magnetic diagnostics foreseen for the Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) stellarator are diamagnetic loops to measure the plasma energy, Rogowski coils to measure the toroidal plasma current, saddle coils to measure the PfirschΓÇôSchl├╝ter currents, segmented Rogowski coils (poloidal magnetic field probes) to add information on the distribution of the plasma current density, and Mirnov coils to observe magnetohydrodynamic modes.

An uninterrupted Rogowski coil surrounds the plasma poloidally, so that the measured change in magnetic flux is directly proportional to the toroidal plasma current.

### Design Goals

Minimization of toroidal currents is in fact one of the major optimization criteria of W7-X. It will be investigated by continuous and segmented Rogowski coils and Saddle coils measuring e.g. bootstrap and Pfirsch-Schlueter currents and their spatial distributions.

The research from the Max-Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP) emphasizes the importance of these diagnostic systems for monitoring plasma behavior during long-pulse operations.

## Overview

The Plasma Liner Experiment (PLX) at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is a platform that seeks to achieve fusion via the Plasma-Jet-Driven Magneto-Inertial Fusion (PJMIF) concept.

## How It Works

The experiment utilizes a constellation of plasma guns to generate fusion-relevant conditions and consists of three main phases: (1) target formation, in which up to four plasma guns shoot magnetized hydrogen or deuterium-tritium jets to form a quasi-spherical target, (2) liner formation, in which a 36 guns fire high-atomic-number (e.g., xenon) jets to form a liner shell, and (3) target compression, in which the formed liner implodes the pre-formed target.

## 2026 Commercialization Effort

LANL is seeking commercialization partners for the Plasma Liner Experiment (PLX), an advanced research platform designed to explore fusion energy and other high-energy plasma applications. Partners are expected to relocate PLX from The Laboratory and establish operations by June 30, 2026.

## Technical Status

PLX is currently at Technology Readiness Level 3 with patents pending. PLX uses synchronized supersonic plasma jets to form imploding plasma liners. This approach enables research and testing without large magnets or multi-megajoule lasers. The platform is modular, compact, and designed for repeatable, non-destructive experiments.

More information is available at lanl.gov/plx.

# 04 ΓÇö Application and collaboration strategy

Stage 40 (`40_applications_collaboration`). Model/effort: Sonnet 5 (xhigh),
per `MODEL_POLICY.md` ("substantial judgment, but bounded by the
Fable-reviewed technical analysis"). Source IDs (`Hxxx`, `Rxxx`, `Pxxx`)
cite `outputs\01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv`; claim IDs (`Cxx`) cite
`outputs\01_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv`; `CASE x` / gates `G0`ΓÇô`G5` / tiers `T0`ΓÇô`T3`
cite `outputs\02_OBSERVABILITY_AND_IDENTIFIABILITY.md` and
`outputs\03_RADIATION_COMPENSATION_ARCHITECTURE.md`. Labels: **Observed /
Derived / Inferred / Proposed / Unknown** per `CLAUDE.md`.

**No contact, submission, or external write occurred in producing this
document.** Every "scientific ask" below is explicitly a non-sent outline,
labeled **PROPOSED, NOT SENT**, per `MISSION.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

---

## 1. Scope and inherited constraints

This stage does not re-derive technical feasibility; it applies the
vetoes already proven in stages 20 and 30 to six candidate application
lanes and scores what remains. Two hard constraints from prior stages
bind every judgment here:

1. **Stage 20 (Theorem 1):** an unreferenced Hall+coil pair can never
   identify absolute scale or Hall offset; only specific engineered
   anchors (machine-current + field model, zero-field epochs, embedded
   calibration winding, material-diverse witness) restore
   identifiability, and each anchor has a stated cost and failure mode
   (`02_MUTUAL_CALIBRATION_FEASIBILITY.md` ┬º2ΓÇô3).
2. **Stage 30 (┬º9.4, binding):** tiers T0ΓÇôT2 (simulation, bench truth,
   self-test hybrid) involve no radiation exposure and constitute the
   complete architecture-validation content relevant to the user's
   current first-author HSX work. Tier T3 (environmental qualification)
   is collaborator-led and is **never** a prerequisite for any HSX
   deliverable. This stage's recommendations preserve that boundary: no
   application recommendation below asks the user to acquire a radiation
   experiment.

An application "wins" here only if it clears the calibration-path and
simpler-alternative vetoes stated in `DECISION_FRAMEWORK.md` ΓÇö a large
market or a famous facility cannot override those vetoes (mission rule).

---

## 2. Scoring rubric (scale and weights)

`outputs\04_APPLICATION_SCORECARD.csv` has no `notes` column, so the
rubric is recorded here per the stage instruction ("show scoring
scale/weights in notes or the collaboration document").

Each of six sub-criteria is scored **0ΓÇô5, 5 = most favorable**:

- `hybrid_value` ΓÇö technical fit of the DC(Hall)+AC(coil) complementarity
  for this application (`DECISION_FRAMEWORK.md` criterion 2).
- `identifiability_path` ΓÇö whether a stage-20 CASE anchor is realistically
  available (criterion 4).
- `radiation_fit` ΓÇö whether the architecture's radiation-compensation
  contribution is actually relevant to this application's stressor
  (criterion 3). Where radiation is not the dominant/relevant stressor by
  design (e.g. the user's own HSX work, or a cryogenic-dominated
  application), this is scored **3/5 "neutral/not-applicable-by-design"**
  rather than penalized ΓÇö absence of a radiation requirement is not a
  technical weakness for a lane that never needed one.
- `experimental_access` ΓÇö realistic access within 24 months (criterion 6).
- `publication_value` ΓÇö criterion 7.
- `collaboration_leverage` ΓÇö criterion 8.

Two more sub-criteria are scored **0ΓÇô5, but 5 = LEAST favorable** (highest
cost / highest risk) and are **inverted** (`5 ΓêÆ score`) before averaging:

- `prototype_cost` (criterion 9).
- `thesis_dilution_risk` (criterion 10).

Composite scores:

```text
technical_score  = mean(hybrid_value, identifiability_path, radiation_fit)
strategic_score  = mean(experimental_access, publication_value,
                         collaboration_leverage,
                         5 ΓêÆ prototype_cost, 5 ΓêÆ thesis_dilution_risk)
overall priority = mean(technical_score, strategic_score)   [ranking only]
```

Novelty-after-prior-art (criterion 5) is not a separate numeric column
because it acts as a **veto**, not a weight, in three of six lanes
(accelerator magnets C29, tacit in the "mature prior art" framing for
SC/HTS C28); per `DECISION_FRAMEWORK.md`, "a high score cannot override
ΓÇª direct prior art that removes the proposed novelty." Vetoes are recorded
in the `veto` column and always win regardless of the numeric scores.

**Overall priority ranking (for reference; full justification per lane in
┬º4 and in `04_APPLICATION_SCORECARD.csv`):**

| Rank | Application | technical_score | strategic_score | veto |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stellarator field mapping (HSX-class) | 3.7 | 4.0 | none |
| 2 | Tokamak long-pulse | 4.0 | 3.4 | none |
| 3 | Accelerator magnets | 1.7 | 2.2 | yes ΓÇö novelty (C29) |
| 4 | Superconducting/HTS magnets, motors/generators | 1.7 | 1.8 | yes ΓÇö structural (C28) |
| 5 | Magneto-inertial fusion/plasma-jet | 1.3 | 1.0 | partial (C35) |
| 6 | Z-pinch/pulsed power | 1.0 | 1.2 | yes ΓÇö no-advantage + no-path (C30) |

---

## 3. Ranked recommendation summary

| Rank | Application | Recommendation | Why (one line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stellarator field mapping | **Approach-now (internal)** | The user's own facility; zero external-access barrier; the necessary T1/T2 validation venue every other lane depends on. |
| 2 | Tokamak long-pulse | **Approach-after-bench-proof** | Strongest external precedent (C02/C27) and sharpest open gap (C06), but reverse-direction and radiation claims are unproven ΓÇö needs a bench result first. |
| 3 | Accelerator magnets | **Monitor** (technique only) | Mature prior art vetoes the architecture (C29); the in-situ rotating-coil self-calibration technique (P057) is already absorbed by citation into stage 30 ┬º5.5. |
| 4 | Superconducting/HTS magnets, motors/generators | **Monitor** (data only) | Structural veto (C28: coil blind to a static trapped field); cryogenic Hall temperature-coefficient literature (P050/P051) is reusable by citation. |
| 5 | Magneto-inertial fusion/plasma-jet | **Do-not-prioritize** | Probes already abandoned in the highest-stress region (C35); boundary niche unevidenced. |
| 6 | Z-pinch/pulsed power | **Do-not-prioritize** | Community solved redundancy without Hall (C30); no persistent DC baseline within a shot. |

---

## 4. Per-application detail

### 4.1 Stellarator field mapping ΓÇö approach-now (internal)

This is not an "approach another group" case in the ordinary sense: the
execution venue is the user's own HSX facility and existing UW-Madison
collaboration (Goodman, Gallenberger, Geiger), already funded as projects
02/03. **Recommendation:** proceed with the planned HSX MVD hardware
install (target August 2026) as stage-30 tier T1; no outreach question is
gated on this stage.

- **Prerequisites (internal):** stage-30 **G0** (T0 simulation honesty
  test, in progress this mission) before **G1** (bench-repeatable
  anchored-hybrid calibration, ΓëÑ3 cycles within predicted uncertainty;
  `╬▒_S`, `╬▓_b` characterized).
- **External monitoring only:** the Wendelstein 7-X MHD Research Unit
  (IPP Greifswald, `outputs\04_COLLABORATOR_CANDIDATES.csv` rank 3) is a
  benchmarking-only candidate ΓÇö no stated need for a Hall+coil hybrid
  exists in their literature (C32), so any future contact should be
  scoped narrowly to comparing trim-coil/error-field correction workflows
  after the user has an HSX-side G1 result to offer, not before.
- **Risk/fallback:** the main risk is treating this lane's low external-
  collaboration score (2/5) as a weakness ΓÇö it is not; it reflects that
  the primary partner is already in place. If the HSX install slips past
  August 2026, the tokamak lane's "approach-after-bench-proof" gate slips
  with it, since G1 evidence is meant to be demonstrated here first.

### 4.2 Tokamak long-pulse ΓÇö approach-after-bench-proof

"""Stage-30 output validator (reusable; mirrors tools/validate_10d_outputs.py).

Checks:
  1. All three stage-30 outputs exist and are nontrivial.
  2. Risk register parses, has the exact required header, unique risk_ids.
  3. Every evidence_id in the register resolves to a ledger source_id or an
     evidence-map claim_id.
  4. Every bracketed [Hxxx]/[Rxxx]/[Pxxx] source ID and every Cxx claim ID
     cited in the two stage-30 markdown files resolves likewise.
  5. Register enumerations (likelihood/impact/decision_gate) use the allowed
     vocabularies.
"""
import csv
import os
import re
import sys

BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
OUT = os.path.join(BASE, "outputs")

REQUIRED_HEADER = [
    "risk_id", "component", "mechanism", "radiation_or_environment",
    "observable_effect", "detectability", "compensation_possible",
    "reference_required", "likelihood", "impact", "evidence_ids",
    "mitigation", "validation_test", "residual_risk", "decision_gate",
]

FILES = {
    "arch": os.path.join(OUT, "03_RADIATION_COMPENSATION_ARCHITECTURE.md"),
    "plan": os.path.join(OUT, "03_SIMULATION_AND_VALIDATION_PLAN.md"),
    "risk": os.path.join(OUT, "03_RADIATION_RISK_REGISTER.csv"),
}

LIKELIHOOD_VOCAB_PREFIX = ("low", "medium", "high", "unknown")
IMPACT_VOCAB_PREFIX = ("low", "medium", "high", "unknown")
GATE_RE = re.compile(r"^G[0-7]$")

failures = []
checks = 0


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    global checks
    checks += 1
    status = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"[{status}] {name}" + (f" ΓÇö {detail}" if detail else ""))
    if not ok:
        failures.append(name)


def load_valid_ids():
    ids = set()
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            ids.add(row["source_id"].strip())
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "01_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            ids.add(row["claim_id"].strip())
    return ids


def main():
    valid_ids = load_valid_ids()
    print(f"loaded {len(valid_ids)} valid source+claim IDs")

    # 1. existence / nontriviality
    for key, path in FILES.items():
        exists = os.path.isfile(path)
        size = os.path.getsize(path) if exists else 0
        check(f"{key} exists and nontrivial", exists and size > 2000,
              f"{os.path.basename(path)} size={size}")

    # 2. register parse + header + uniqueness
    with open(FILES["risk"], encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        reader = csv.reader(f)
        header = next(reader)
        rows = list(reader)
    check("register header exact", header == REQUIRED_HEADER,
          "match" if header == REQUIRED_HEADER else f"got {header}")
    check("register row count", len(rows) >= 15, f"{len(rows)} rows")
    ids = [r[0] for r in rows]
    check("risk_id unique", len(ids) == len(set(ids)))
    check("all rows full-width", all(len(r) == len(REQUIRED_HEADER) for r in rows))

    # 3. evidence_ids resolve
    idx = REQUIRED_HEADER.index("evidence_ids")
    bad = []
    for r in rows:
        for eid in r[idx].split(";"):
            eid = eid.strip()
            if eid and eid not in valid_ids:
                bad.append((r[0], eid))
    check("register evidence_ids resolve", not bad, f"unresolved: {bad}" if bad else "all resolve")

    # 4. enum vocab + gates
    li = REQUIRED_HEADER.index("likelihood")
    im = REQUIRED_HEADER.index("impact")
    dg = REQUIRED_HEADER.index("decision_gate")
    bad_enum = [r[0] for r in rows
                if not r[li].startswith(LIKELIHOOD_VOCAB_PREFIX)
                or not r[im].startswith(IMPACT_VOCAB_PREFIX)
                or not GATE_RE.match(r[dg])]
    check("register enums/gates valid", not bad_enum, str(bad_enum) if bad_enum else "ok")

    # 5. markdown citations resolve
    id_re = re.compile(r"\[([HRP]\d{3})\]")
    claim_re = re.compile(r"\bC\d{2}\b")
    for key in ("arch", "plan"):
        text = open(FILES[key], encoding="utf-8").read()
        cited = set(id_re.findall(text))
        claims = set(c for c in claim_re.findall(text))
        bad_src = sorted(c for c in cited if c not in valid_ids)
        bad_claim = sorted(c for c in claims if c not in valid_ids)
        check(f"{key} source IDs resolve ({len(cited)} cited)", not bad_src,
              f"unresolved: {bad_src}" if bad_src else "all resolve")
        check(f"{key} claim IDs resolve ({len(claims)} cited)", not bad_claim,
              f"unresolved: {bad_claim}" if bad_claim else "all resolve")

    print(f"\n{checks - len(failures)}/{checks} checks passed")
    if failures:
        print("FAILURES:", failures)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Stage-40 output validator (reusable; mirrors tools/validate_30_outputs.py).

Checks:
  1. All three stage-40 outputs exist and are nontrivial.
  2. Both CSVs parse, have the exact required header from the stage prompt,
     correct row counts, unique application/rank values.
  3. Every ID cited in evidence_ids / relevant_publication_ids (Cxx claim IDs;
     Hxxx/Rxxx/Pxxx source IDs) resolves against the stage-10D ledger/map.
  4. Every bare Cxx / Hxxx / Rxxx / Pxxx token cited in the prose strategy
     document resolves likewise.
  5. veto column non-empty for every row that the scorecard's recommendation
     marks do-not-prioritize, and rank values are a 1..N permutation.
  6. No outreach/contact-detail leakage: strategy doc contains no email
     addresses or phone-number-shaped strings.
"""
import csv
import os
import re
import sys

BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
OUT = os.path.join(BASE, "outputs")

SCORECARD_HEADER = [
    "application", "problem", "incumbent_diagnostic", "hybrid_value",
    "identifiability_path", "radiation_fit", "experimental_access",
    "publication_value", "collaboration_leverage", "prototype_cost",
    "thesis_dilution_risk", "technical_score", "strategic_score", "veto",
    "evidence_ids", "rank", "recommendation", "next_gate",
]

CANDIDATES_HEADER = [
    "rank", "group_or_facility", "institution", "application", "official_url",
    "relevant_publication_ids", "unique_capability", "proposed_scientific_ask",
    "prerequisites", "access_uncertainty", "competition_or_ip_risk", "phd_fit",
    "recommendation", "notes",
]

FILES = {
    "scorecard": os.path.join(OUT, "04_APPLICATION_SCORECARD.csv"),
    "strategy": os.path.join(OUT, "04_COLLABORATION_STRATEGY.md"),
    "candidates": os.path.join(OUT, "04_COLLABORATOR_CANDIDATES.csv"),
}

failures = []
checks = 0


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    global checks
    checks += 1
    status = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"[{status}] {name}" + (f" ΓÇö {detail}" if detail else ""))
    if not ok:
        failures.append(name)


def load_valid_ids():
    ids = set()
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            ids.add(row["source_id"].strip())
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "01_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            ids.add(row["claim_id"].strip())
    return ids


def read_csv_rows(path, required_header):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        reader = csv.reader(f)
        header = next(reader)
        rows = list(reader)
    return header, rows


def main():
    valid_ids = load_valid_ids()
    print(f"loaded {len(valid_ids)} valid source+claim IDs")

    for key, path in FILES.items():
        exists = os.path.isfile(path)
        size = os.path.getsize(path) if exists else 0
        check(f"{key} exists and nontrivial", exists and size > 1500,
              f"{os.path.basename(path)} size={size}")

    # Scorecard checks
    sc_header, sc_rows = read_csv_rows(FILES["scorecard"], SCORECARD_HEADER)
    check("scorecard header exact", sc_header == SCORECARD_HEADER,
          "match" if sc_header == SCORECARD_HEADER else f"got {sc_header}")
    check("scorecard row count == 6", len(sc_rows) == 6, f"{len(sc_rows)} rows")
    check("scorecard rows full-width",
          all(len(r) == len(SCORECARD_HEADER) for r in sc_rows))
    apps = [r[0] for r in sc_rows]
    check("scorecard application values unique", len(apps) == len(set(apps)))
    ranks = sorted(int(r[SCORECARD_HEADER.index("rank")]) for r in sc_rows)
    check("scorecard rank is 1..N permutation", ranks == list(range(1, len(sc_rows) + 1)),
          str(ranks))
    veto_idx = SCORECARD_HEADER.index("veto")
    rec_idx = SCORECARD_HEADER.index("recommendation")
    dnp_no_veto = [r[0] for r in sc_rows
                   if r[rec_idx].startswith("do-not-prioritize") and r[veto_idx].strip().lower().startswith("none")]
    check("every do-not-prioritize row states a veto", not dnp_no_veto,
          str(dnp_no_veto) if dnp_no_veto else "ok")

    ev_idx = SCORECARD_HEADER.index("evidence_ids")
    bad = []
    for r in sc_rows:
        for eid in r[ev_idx].split(";"):
            eid = eid.strip()
            if eid and eid not in valid_ids:
                bad.append((r[0], eid))
    check("scorecard evidence_ids resolve", not bad, f"unresolved: {bad}" if bad else "all resolve")

    # Candidates checks
    cd_header, cd_rows = read_csv_rows(FILES["candidates"], CANDIDATES_HEADER)
    check("candidates header exact", cd_header == CANDIDATES_HEADER,
          "match" if cd_header == CANDIDATES_HEADER else f"got {cd_header}")
    check("candidates row count == 10", len(cd_rows) == 10, f"{len(cd_rows)} rows")
    check("candidates rows full-width",
          all(len(r) == len(CANDIDATES_HEADER) for r in cd_rows))
    cranks = sorted(int(r[0]) for r in cd_rows)
    check("candidates rank is 1..N permutation", cranks == list(range(1, len(cd_rows) + 1)),
          str(cranks))
    groups = [r[1] for r in cd_rows]
    check("candidates group_or_facility unique", len(groups) == len(set(groups)))

    pub_idx = CANDIDATES_HEADER.index("relevant_publication_ids")
    bad2 = []
    id_token_re = re.compile(r"\b([CHRP]\d{2,3})\b")
    for r in cd_rows:
        for tok in id_token_re.findall(r[pub_idx]):
            if tok not in valid_ids:
                bad2.append((r[1], tok))
    check("candidates relevant_publication_ids resolve", not bad2,
          f"unresolved: {bad2}" if bad2 else "all resolve")

    # ask discipline: every proposed_scientific_ask must say PROPOSED, NOT SENT
    ask_idx = CANDIDATES_HEADER.index("proposed_scientific_ask")
    bad_ask = [r[1] for r in cd_rows if "PROPOSED, NOT SENT" not in r[ask_idx]]
    check("every candidate ask labeled PROPOSED, NOT SENT", not bad_ask,
          str(bad_ask) if bad_ask else "ok")

    # Strategy doc: citation resolution + no contact-detail leakage
    text = open(FILES["strategy"], encoding="utf-8").read()
    cited = set(id_token_re.findall(text))
    bad3 = sorted(c for c in cited if c not in valid_ids and not re.match(r"^G[0-9]$", c))
    # filter out gate-like tokens (G0-G5) and tier tokens (T0-T3) misfired by regex (won't match [CHRP] anyway)
    check(f"strategy doc source/claim IDs resolve ({len(cited)} tokens)", not bad3,
          f"unresolved: {bad3}" if bad3 else "all resolve")

    email_re = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+")
    phone_re = re.compile(r"\b\d{3}[-.\s]\d{3}[-.\s]\d{4}\b")
    emails = email_re.findall(text)
    phones = phone_re.findall(text)
    check("strategy doc has no email addresses", not emails, str(emails) if emails else "none found")
    check("strategy doc has no phone-shaped strings", not phones, str(phones) if phones else "none found")

    # same check on the two CSVs (concatenate raw text)
    csv_text = (open(FILES["scorecard"], encoding="utf-8").read() +
                open(FILES["candidates"], encoding="utf-8").read())
    emails2 = email_re.findall(csv_text)
    check("CSVs have no email addresses", not emails2, str(emails2) if emails2 else "none found")

    print(f"\n{checks - len(failures)}/{checks} checks passed")
    if failures:
        print("FAILURES:", failures)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
